title: National AI Skilling Initiative Records 60,253 Enrolments in Phase I; IICT and Private Sector Partners have Jointly Developed Curriculum to Equip Students with Industry-Relevant AI Skills
body_text:
The total number of applications received, and participants enrolled under Phase I of the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Skilling Initiative as on date is 60,253.
The total number of participants who have completed 2 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 4620 and those who have completed all 4 Modules of Phase I of the programme are 552.
Phase I of the programme comprises four modules with a total duration of 33 hours, delivered through two learning platforms. The details of the Modules of Phase I are as under: -
Platform 1:
Module 1: AI Essentials – gain practical skills to boost daily productivity, synthesize data, and create content. Module 2: Prompting Essentials – framework to write professional prompts.
Platform 2:
Module 3: Introduction to Generative AI – grasp Large Language Model (LLM) fundamentals and responsible AI guidelines. Module 4: Generative AI Leader – master workflow automation and strategic Gen AI organisational transformation.
The details of Phase II, including the curriculum, modules and course duration, are under finalisation.
The curriculum has been jointly designed and developed by the IICT and private sector partners to impart foundational and practical AI skills. The advanced skilling component is conducted by IICT for joint certification.
The Government’s role has been to provide strategic direction and facilitating the implementation of the programme through IICT with the objective of enhancing AI literacy and equipping students with industry-relevant digital skills.
The information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to a Question asked by Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi in Lok Sabha today.
****
Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, MoS Dr. L. Murugan stated that Phase I of the National AI Skilling Initiative has recorded 60,253 applications/enrolments, with 4,620 participants completing 2 modules and 552 completing all 4 modules. Phase I comprises four modules (33 hours total) across two learning platforms covering AI Essentials, Prompting Essentials, Introduction to Generative AI, and Generative AI Leader. The curriculum was jointly developed by IICT and private sector partners, with Phase II details still under finalisation.
enrichment.context:
The National AI Skilling Initiative reflects India's broader push to build AI literacy and a skilled digital workforce as part of the IndiaAI Mission, which aims to democratize AI access, build compute infrastructure, and develop human capital for AI adoption across sectors. IICT (Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs is not the expansion here; in this context IICT refers to an implementing training institute) partnering with private industry players signals a public-private model similar to skilling programmes like Skill India, where government provides strategic direction while industry partners bring domain expertise and joint certification lends credibility for employability.

This initiative is significant against the backdrop of global competition in AI talent development and India's aspiration to be a leading AI hub, as reiterated in Union Budget announcements and the IndiaAI Mission's skilling pillar. Written replies in Parliament on such programmes also serve as an accountability mechanism, allowing scrutiny of enrolment versus completion rates (here, completion rate of all 4 modules is less than 1% of enrolments), which could raise questions about programme design, learner engagement, and last-mile delivery of digital skilling schemes in India.

prelims_questions.question: The National AI Skilling Initiative discussed in a Lok Sabha reply is implemented under the strategic direction of which entity, in partnership with private sector players?

prelims_questions.question: How many modules does Phase I of the National AI Skilling Initiative comprise, and what is its total duration?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states Phase I comprises four modules with a total duration of 33 hours, delivered through two learning platforms.
